findings.reason: the plan should either declare codex the owner of the EDDB extractor or name the shared-remote-core extraction, instead of forking ~5k lines that will drift.
findings.text: the plan's §3 remote extractor ("a stdlib-plus-wrapper script executed over ssh, niced, that takes a batch of (shot, category, dname) requests on stdin and streams compact binary arrays back", plan.html:207-211) reproduces the subsystem owned by imas-codex/remote/: executor.py (1365 lines), ssh_worker.py (898, the persistent ssh pool that amortizes the ~2.6 s session setup), serialization.py (114, the msgpack array wire format), and locations.py/tools.py carry the per-host nice registry the plan's "niced" mirrors; imas_codex/remote/scripts/enumerate_edas.py is already the JT-60SA EDDB-over-ssh script. The plan names the owner only as "the codex remote executor" (no file) and justifies the fork with one line ("ambix must not require codex at runtime", plan.html:210-212) without weighing extracting the facility-agnostic remote core (5,241 lines) into a package both repos import.

findings.reason: a second literal mirror root is exactly the duplication the owner exists to prevent, and adding JT60SA_ROOT beside MIRROR_ROOT is a one-line change the plan should name.
findings.text: §3 and the mirror-location decision hardcode the JT-60SA cache root as a literal "/work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa" (plan.html:229,544) rather than declaring it in imas_ambix/data/paths.py, whose own docstring (paths.py:3-4) states it is "the single source of truth — every other module imports from here so we don't accidentally hardcode the mirror layout in multiple places" and which already holds MIRROR_ROOT for the MAST store. The plan names no owner for the new root.

findings.reason: the section must account for the interface surface it adds in its own text, per the one rule the interface budget imposes.
findings.text: §2 adds a tokamap exporter, §3 a remote extractor and §7 an EQDB reader (new public definitions; supplied counts public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0); none of these sections names what it retires or merges, and none states why nothing can be.

duplicate_owner-1.reason: Acted in later plan versions: section 3 names imas_codex/remote (executor.py, ssh_worker.py, serialization.py) as the owner it does not extend, states why (the codex distribution drags neo4j, fastmcp, rapidfuzz, lxml and pypdf onto ambix's runtime path) and defers a shared core to the second facility. This answer replaces a section 5 reason misapplied to this record on 2026-10-06, when review-plan --answer resolved the newest record by file mtime and a bulk store had just made this version-7 record the newest.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new capability layers on existing deep modules (machine_map schema, transform engine, description reader, virtual zarr view, cocos_convention scorer) through their existing interfaces; the plan adds distinct capabilities (extractor, cache writer, census, tokamap export, EQDB reader) rather than a spread of shallow wrappers over one mechanism.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the §3 remote extractor re-implements the remote-execution subsystem owned by imas-codex/remote/ (executor.py, ssh_worker.py, serialization.py), and the cache root bypasses imas_ambix/data/paths.py, the declared single source of truth for mirror paths.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 (§2 adds a tokamap exporter), §3 (a remote extractor) and §7 (an EQDB reader) add public definitions without naming what they retire or merge, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched imas-ambix, imas-codex, nakamap and nova and cites the mechanisms it layers on: transform_machine_description and geometry_table_from_description (imas_ambix/data/description_reader.py:23-102), the zarr and netCDF store engines (imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:140,234), VirtualZarrView (imas_ambix/data/virtual_zarr.py), the MAST geometry transitions (imas_ambix/data/geometry_transitions.py), and the codex EDAS scanner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two wrapping proposals each state why the existing machinery cannot be extended: tokamap has no slot for units, sign, COCOS or evidence, so ambix-schema is authoritative with a lossless forward export, and the extractor is owned by ambix because the runtime must not depend on imas-codex.
